answers.solution:
I reproduced all four failure modes, implemented the structural merge fix, and verified it end-to-end. The full self-contained document is at **`/workspace/SOLUTION.md`** (708 lines), with the tested tool source at `/workspace/wavemerge-src/main.go` and `/workspace/union_additive.py`.

## What I did

Built a minimal Go repo (`/workspace/repro`) with a shared `server.go` and created 4 feature branches that each add a mux registration, a handler func, and a `case` inside the existing `isV2EnvelopeRoutePath`. Then reproduced each symptom against real `git merge` output.

## Root causes (all reproduced)

1. **Shared trailing `}`** — the conflict hunk ends inside OURS's new func; git shows the closing `}` as shared context, so union leaves `handleA` unclosed:
   ```
   server.go:31:6: expected '(', found handleB
   ```
2. **Interleaved 3-way diff** — a text union splices two funcs together.
3. **Dropped intra-declaration hunk** — a `case` added inside `isV2EnvelopeRoutePath` is lost by "new decls + mux line" extractors. The tree **builds**, and only the envelope test fails.
4. **Stale sibling control** — a branch test asserting `GET /experimental/b == 404` fails once `b` lands (got 200).

## The fix

`wavemerge` (`go/parser` + `go/ast`): keeps ours verbatim, then splices in only what the branch *added* — new top-level decls (with doc comments), added runs **inside pre-existing declarations** anchored by up to 3 preceding common lines, and imported-spec union. It **exits 1 if an added run can't be anchored**, so nothing is dropped silently.

Per-branch runbook:
```bash
# gate the branch first: gofmt -l, go build ./..., go vet ./..., package tests
git show main:server.go      > /tmp/base.go
git show "$BRANCH":server.go > /tmp/theirs.go
go run ./tools/wavemerge -base /tmp/base.go -ours server.go -theirs /tmp/theirs.go -out server.go
# repeat for server_test.go, then:
gofmt -w server.go server_test.go
go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./internal/shim/opencode/...
```
Plus: rewrite stale sibling-404 controls to assert the sibling's own contract, and regenerate declared-vs-served JSON/YAML from the merged tree.

## Verification (all executed)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Naive union, 2 branches | syntax error (reproduced) |
| Dropped intra-decl hunk | `BUILD OK`, `TestEnvelope_handleB` FAIL (reproduced) |
| Brace-aware union (`union_additive.py`) | `BUILD OK`, `TestEnvelope_handleA` FAIL — proves build is not enough |
| `wavemerge` 4-branch wave `a,b,c,d` | each merge: build OK, vet OK, package tests OK |
| Import union (`httptest` added by branch D) | grouped import correct |
| Stale control rewrite | `ALL PACKAGE TESTS GREEN` |
| Final gate on `wave-struct` | `gofmt` clean, build OK, vet OK, tests OK |
| Embedded tool in markdown | byte-identical to tested source, `gofmt` clean, builds |

The document includes the full 345-line tool, the Python brace-fixer, the exact conflict/failure outputs, a runbook checklist, and known limitations (additive-only; loud failure on true edits).

signatures.description:
SYMPTOM: merging several independent feature branches that each ADD a route registration and a new handler to the SAME Go file (server.go) in one wave. `git merge --no-ff` conflicts; resolving with 'keep both sides' (union) produces files that do not compile: (a) the conflict hunk ends inside the OURS function body and the closing brace is shared trailing context, so the union duplicates it once — ours' function is left unclosed ('syntax error: unexpected name http in argument list'); (b) with 3+ branches the 3-way diff INTERLEAVES the new function of theirs with existing declarations, so a text union splices two functions together. A second, quieter failure: when you extract a branch's additions programmatically (new top-level decls + mux registration run) and apply them to ours, any added lines that live INSIDE a PRE-EXISTING declaration are silently dropped. In this case the branch also added a branch inside the existing isV2EnvelopeRoutePath func; the merged tree compiled and 200+ tests ran, but the one test that asserted the declared 401 envelope failed (v1 UNAUTHENTICATED body instead of the v2 UnauthorizedError envelope) — the dropped hunk was invisible until the suite ran.

ROOT CAUSE: Go files are not line-independent. A conflict region's shared trailing '}' closes exactly one of the two appended functions; union keeps one '}'. And additions are not all top-level: an added line can extend an existing function's dispatch table, envelope map, or switch. Any merge tool that reasons line-wise or 'declaration-wise' without accounting for intra-declaration additions will compile only by luck.

FIX (proven on a 6-branch wave): (1) prefer 'both sides kept' ONLY for hunk-1-style pure additions (route registration comments + one mux line) where both sides are lexically complete; (2) for hunks where the OURS side ends inside a function body, insert the missing closing brace between the sides explicitly, then gofmt+build to prove it; (3) for the harder interleavings, do a STRUCTURAL merge: keep ours verbatim, extract the branch's (a) added mux-registration run, (b) NEW top-level declarations (parse '^func ' ... closing '}' at column 0, plus doc comments), and (c) any added runs inside PRE-EXISTING declarations — locate each by its diff context anchor and insert it there (this third class is the one that silently disappears); (4) after every merge run the affected PACKAGE suites (not just build) because a dropped intra-function hunk compiles fine; (5) regenerate any machine-generated artifact (declared-vs-served JSON) from the MERGED tree instead of merging the artifact textually.

VERIFICATION: per-branch gates before merging (go build ./..., go vet, package tests, gofmt); per-merge merged-tree re-gate; the final full short suite on main. Two real defects were caught this way: a []byte-vs-string compile error in a cross-branch test control, and the dropped isV2EnvelopeRoutePath branch (caught by its 401-envelope test). Also: a test written on a branch may assert the PRE-MERGE state of a sibling ('sibling route must still 404'); when the sibling row lands in the same wave the control must be rewritten to assert the sibling answers its OWN contract (e.g. body contains the parent's payload key), not a 404.
